turn.content: The records settle it. The contract fixes VAT at 11%; the invoice applied 12% (6,491,510 × ... i.e. 649,812 = 12% of 5,415,100), and code confirmed the invoicing falls outside the received value only by that overstated tax.

tool_calls.name: submit_report
tool_calls.arguments: {"diagnoses": [{"issue_code": "tax_mismatch", "line": null, "cause": "wrong_tax_rate", "evidence": [{"kind": "invoice", "ref": "INV-000459", "detail": "Tax charged 649812.0 on a subtotal of 5415100.0, i.e. 12% rather than the 11% the contract specifies (11% would be 595661.0)."}, {"kind": "contract_clause", "ref": "KTR-V-002#3.1", "detail": "Each invoice carries VAT at 11% of the subtotal, which is the tax base."}, {"kind": "purchase_order", "ref": "PO-2026-0122", "detail": "Ordered 3 Dual-Band Wireless Routers at 1283700 and 1 External SSD 1TB at 1564000; invoice unit prices match, so the subtotal itself is correct and only the tax is off."}], "explanation": "The invoice applied a 12% VAT rate to the subtotal, whereas clause KTR-V-002#3.1 of the vendor's contract fixes VAT at 11% of the subtotal, overstating tax by 54,151.0 (649,812.0 instead of 595,661.0)."}]}
